Parties: we represent The Associated Press; counterparty is Kubient Inc..

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

content.text: No audit, inspection, or verification right binding the Customer appears anywhere in the Agreement. Since this rule is defensive — limiting audits of *our* usage — its absence is favorable to us.

input.quote: Customer agrees to provide all reasonable and necessary access, support and cooperation for Kubient to provide the Services in a timely and effective manner.
input.rationale: Searches for "audit", "inspect", "records" and "verif" returned no hits, and a full read of the single operative section (§§ 1–14) confirms Kubient is granted no audit, inspection, or usage-verification right against The Associated Press. The only access language (p0001) is ordinary cooperation for Kubient to deliver the Services, not a right to audit AP's usage, books, or systems; the use restrictions in § 6 and the confidentiality provisions in § 12 likewise contain no inspection or self-certification mechanic, and there is no remote or on-site system-access right. Because this rule is protective of the customer, the absence of any audit right binding us is at or better than the preferred position (limited frequency, notice, off-site, vendor-cost audits), so no redline is required. Note for a separate rule: Impressions are "as measured by Kubient" (p0009) with no verification right in AP's favour — that is an audit right we may want *against* the vendor, outside the direction of this rule.

content.text:
**Finding: compliant — no redline proposed.**

The Agreement contains no audit, inspection, or verification right running against The Associated Press:

- Literal searches for "audit", "inspect", "records" and "verif" returned zero hits.
- A full read of the document's single operative section (§§ 1–14, p0000–p0074) confirms no clause lets Kubient examine our books, usage, or systems.
- The only access-flavoured language is § 1's ordinary cooperation covenant ("Customer agrees to provide all reasonable and necessary access, support and cooperation for Kubient to provide the Services"), which is service-delivery cooperation, not an audit right. § 6 (Use of Service) imposes use restrictions but no self-certification or inspection mechanic, and § 12 (Confidentiality) contains no audit hook.

Because AUDIT is a defensive rule, absence of any audit right is better than the preferred position (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, vendor cost, no system access), so no edit is warranted.

One flag for a different rule (opposite direction, so not redlined here): § 3(e) defines Impressions as measured **by Kubient**, and § 5 revenue share depends on Kubient's collections, yet AP has no right to verify Kubient's measurement or payment records. If your playbook has a vendor-side records/audit rule, that gap is worth pursuing there.

input.rationale: No audit right binding the Customer exists in this Agreement, so there is nothing for the AUDIT rule to constrain and no redline is warranted. Literal searches for "audit", "inspect", "records", "verif", "examine" and "books" returned zero hits, and a full read of the single operative section (§§ 1-14, p0000-p0074) confirms Kubient has no right to audit, inspect or verify AP's usage, books, systems or accounts. Every "access" reference is unrelated to auditing: p0001 is an ordinary cooperation/access covenant so Kubient can deliver the Services; p0002 is AP's inbound licence to the Auction Platform; p0025 restricts AP from granting third-party access to the Service; and p0035/p0045 are database-security representations. There is accordingly no on-site or remote system-access audit right, no self-certification mechanic in § 6 (Use of Service), and no inspection hook in § 12 (Confidentiality). Because AUDIT is protective of the customer, this compliance-by-absence sits at or better than the preferred position (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, off-site, Vendor's cost, no system access); the deterministic "audit frequency limited" check fails only because no audit clause exists to carry frequency limits, which is not a defect. Separately noted for a different rule and out of scope here (opposite direction): Impressions are defined as measured by Kubient (p0009) and revenue share depends on Kubient's collections (§ 5), yet AP has no verification right against Kubient - a gap in our favour to pursue under any vendor-side records/audit rule.

input.rationale: Searches for "audit", "inspect", "records" and "verif" returned no hits, and a full read of the single operative section (§§ 1–14) confirms Kubient is granted no audit, inspection, or usage-verification right against The Associated Press. The only access language (p0001) is ordinary cooperation for Kubient to deliver the Services, not a right to audit AP's usage, books, or systems; the use restrictions in § 6 and the confidentiality provisions in § 12 likewise contain no inspection or self-certification mechanic, and there is no remote or on-site system-access right. Because this rule is protective of the customer, the absence of any audit right binding us is at or better than the preferred position (limited frequency, notice, off-site, vendor-cost audits), so no redline is required. Note for a separate rule: Impressions are "as measured by Kubient" (p0009) with no verification right in AP's favour — that is an audit right we may want *against* the vendor, outside the direction of this rule.

content.text:
**Finding: compliant — no redline proposed.**

The Agreement contains no audit, inspection, or verification right running against The Associated Press:

- Literal searches for "audit", "inspect", "records" and "verif" returned zero hits.
- A full read of the document's single operative section (§§ 1–14, p0000–p0074) confirms no clause lets Kubient examine our books, usage, or systems.
- The only access-flavoured language is § 1's ordinary cooperation covenant ("Customer agrees to provide all reasonable and necessary access, support and cooperation for Kubient to provide the Services"), which is service-delivery cooperation, not an audit right. § 6 (Use of Service) imposes use restrictions but no self-certification or inspection mechanic, and § 12 (Confidentiality) contains no audit hook.

Because AUDIT is a defensive rule, absence of any audit right is better than the preferred position (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, vendor cost, no system access), so no edit is warranted.

One flag for a different rule (opposite direction, so not redlined here): § 3(e) defines Impressions as measured **by Kubient**, and § 5 revenue share depends on Kubient's collections, yet AP has no right to verify Kubient's measurement or payment records. If your playbook has a vendor-side records/audit rule, that gap is worth pursuing there.

Separately noted for a different rule and out of scope here (opposite direction): Impressions are defined as measured by Kubient (p0009) and revenue share depends on Kubient's collections (§ 5), yet AP has no verification right against Kubient - a gap in our favour to pursue under any vendor-side records/audit rule.

input.rationale: Searches for "audit", "inspect", "records", "verif", "examine" and "books" return no hits, and a full read of §§ 1-14 confirms the Agreement contains no express audit right against AP: p0001 is service-delivery cooperation, p0002 our inbound licence, p0025 a use-restriction covenant, and p0035/p0045 database-security reps. The rule is therefore unsatisfied by absence rather than by adverse drafting, and I am reporting it as missing rather than compliant so the playbook's parameters actually appear on the page. The reason this is worth an edit: paragraph 6(a) imposes substantive, audit-prone use restrictions on us (no transfer, no third-party access, no reverse engineering, no service-bureau use, privacy-policy requirements) and makes us "responsible and solely liable" for Content and Properties, but is silent on how Kubient may verify compliance. Silence is not protection - it leaves the frequency, notice, cost and system-access questions open to be resolved by demand or by implication, which is the walk-away risk this rule guards against. The redline inserts a new paragraph 6(b) fixing the preferred position with a single minimal insertion and no change to existing text: one verification per twelve months, 30 days' prior written notice, business hours, independent third-party auditor under confidentiality no less protective than paragraph 12, off-site review of records wherever practicable, express exclusion of any direct, remote or on-site access to our systems, networks, databases or facilities, and Kubient's sole cost unless an underpayment by us exceeds 5%. The comment offers the fallback (15 days' notice, 10% threshold). Out of scope for this rule but noted for a vendor-side records rule: Impressions are measured by Kubient (p0009) and revenue share depends on Kubient's collections (§ 5), yet we have no reciprocal verification right - a gap in our favour to pursue separately.

Any such verification shall be conducted off-site by review of records and written responses provided by Customer wherever practicable, shall not include any direct, remote or on-site access to Customer's systems, networks, databases or facilities, and shall be at Kubient's sole cost and expense unless it reveals an underpayment by Customer exceeding five percent (5%) of the amounts properly due.

The Agreement contains no audit, inspection, or verification right running against The Associated Press:

- Literal searches for "audit", "inspect", "records" and "verif" returned zero hits.
- A full read of the document's single operative section (§§ 1–14, p0000–p0074) confirms no clause lets Kubient examine our books, usage, or systems.

{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement (Exhibit 10.14)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Playbook review of the Master Services Agreement dated 5 February (Customer/AP — Kubient) 
**Status:** 19 rules assessed; 17 findings verified, 2 findings failed verification and are held for review

## Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against the playbook. The commercial architecture is unusually favourable to us in several respects: the Vendor indemnity is broad and uncapped, there is no exclusivity, non-compete, MFN, minimum-commitment or Customer-payable liquidated damages exposure, and the fee model is a revenue share rather than committed spend. We recommend no redline on those points.

The issues that warrant negotiation fall into two groups. First, **material gaps** — there is no monetary limitation of liability anywhere in the Agreement, no proprietary rights/ownership article covering deliverables and our data, no post-termination transition assistance or data-return obligation, and no Vendor insurance requirement. Given that Kubient hosts the platform and collects, stores and measures our data, the ownership, transition and insurance gaps are commercially significant. Second, **deviations from our preferred position** — the platform licence is expressly revocable at will and covers the Customer entity only; we have no convenience termination right during the Initial Term while Kubient has a mid-term "for any reason" exit; the post-Initial-Term exit requires 90 days' notice; governing law (Delaware) does not match the agreed New York exclusive venue; Kubient may assign freely, including to a competitor; and Kubient's warranties carry no remedy and no workmanlike standard.

Two findings (non-solicitation and audit rights) failed verification and should not be treated as settled conclusions. In both cases the underlying review reports that the Agreement is silent, and in both cases we would be *creating* a restriction on ourselves by inserting the playbook clause. We do not propose adding a non-solicit. The audit point is discretionary and low priority.

## Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section (as reported) | Verified | Position / action |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | Missing | Preamble | Pass | No monetary cap on direct liability anywhere; add mutual cap at greater of 12 months' amounts or USD 1,000,000, keyed to amounts paid or payable between the Parties (the revenue-share model makes a Customer-fees cap illusory), with uncapped carve-outs and Section 5 payments excluded. |
| 2 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | Preamble | Pass | Broad Vendor indemnity in our favour, uncapped and carved out of the consequential-damages waiver; Customer-side indemnity is reciprocal and symmetric. No redline — reopening risks unravelling a bargain that favours us. |
| 3 | High | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Missing | Preamble | Pass | No proprietary rights article. Add subsection confirming we own our Content, Properties and data; Kubient assigns deliverables with a perpetual royalty-free licence back for embedded Kubient IP; no joint ownership. No adverse assignment of our IP, so no walk-away trigger. |
| 4 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | Preamble | Pass | Licence is "revocable" and runs to the Customer entity only. Extend to affiliates and contractors, delete at-will revocability (revocable only on termination under the termination article), and permit transfer to a successor; retain the no-sublicence restriction. |
